mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a high-inflation regime where real rates do not rise.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a supply shock that offsets demand weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation is simultaneously high.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average, coinciding with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST), signals a synchronized expansion in manufacturing and construction, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-mo MA and HOUST > 12-mo MA simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a demand contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% while the federal funds rate remains above 4.5% signals a disinflationary environment with restrictive policy, which increases term premium and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a simultaneous demand shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above its 6-month average, without a corresponding rise in unemployment, signals robust consumer demand that supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 6-mo MA for 2 consecutive months AND UNRATE stable
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a supply disruption.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payrolls (PAYEMS) month-over-month is inconsistent and signals labor market confusion; this ambiguity increases uncertainty and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a clear recession or strong expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a broad-based supply contraction, which raises input costs and depresses earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a demand surge that offsets supply weakness.
